name: Cyanobacteria
description: The original photosynthetic intelligence — 3.5 billion years of solar energy conversion that oxygenated Earth's atmosphere. Nitrogen fixation in heterocysts creates specialized cellular division of labor. Circadian clock proteins (KaiABC) form the simplest known biological oscillator, maintaining 24-hour rhythm without transcription.

core_attributes.pattern: photosynthetic origin, nitrogen fixation, circadian protein oscillation

scope.definition: Nitrogen fixation rate efficiency of diazotrophic cyanobacteria (Anabaena, Nostoc) — fraction of atmospheric N2 converted to bioavailable NH4+ per unit ATP consumed relative to theoretical minimum.

evidence.source: Postgate (1998) 'Nitrogen Fixation', 3rd ed., Cambridge UP; Rubio & Ludden (2008) 'Biosynthesis of the iron-molybdenum cofactor of nitrogenase', Annual Review of Microbiology 62:93-111.
cross_domain_examples: cyanobacterial nitrogenase converts N2 to NH3 with thermodynamic efficiency 0.92-0.97 per N-N bond broken
Anabaena cylindrica: heterocyst N2 fixation rate 2.5× faster than equivalent free-living diazotrophs
legume-rhizobium nodule: analogous N2 fixation with 60-90% of plant N needs met — eukaryote host version

scope.falsifiability: If cyanobacterial cultures show no measurable N2 reduction under 15N2 labeling conditions, the organism is not fixing atmospheric nitrogen despite nitrogenase gene presence.
scope.measurement_limits: Fixation efficiency requires anoxic microenvironment (heterocysts protect nitrogenase from O2 inactivation). Combined nitrogen (NO3-, NH4+) suppresses nitrogenase expression. Temperature optimum 25-30°C.
